## `CalculationResult`

```python
class CalculationResult(*, provenance: Provenance, warnings: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> None
```

Base class of results. Values are stored unrounded; rounding is for display only.

### `CalculationResult.outputs`

```python
outputs(self) -> tuple[OutputItem, ...]
```

All output values in presentation order.

### `CalculationResult.chart_data`

```python
chart_data(self) -> ChartData | None
```

Data for the default chart of this result, if it has one.

## `ChartData`

```python
class ChartData(title: str, categories: tuple[str, ...], values: tuple[float, ...], unit: str, source: str, kind: "Literal['bar', 'line']" = 'bar', x: tuple[float, ...] = (), x_label: str = '', y_label: str = '') -> None
```

The data behind a result chart, so every interface plots exactly the result.

``kind="bar"`` plots ``values`` against ``categories``. ``kind="line"`` plots
``values`` against the numeric ``x``.

## `Tolerances`

```python
class Tolerances(rel: float = 1e-09, abs: float = 1e-12) -> None
```

Relative and absolute tolerances for approximate comparisons.

The defaults are numerical choices, not physical constants. They sit far
above the rounding error accumulated by the handful of float64 operations
used in the current models (machine epsilon is about 2.2e-16) and far
below any realistic measurement precision. They are recorded in the
provenance of each result and can be overridden by the caller.

### `Tolerances.isclose`

```python
isclose(self, a: float, b: float) -> bool
```

True if ``a`` and ``b`` agree within the relative or absolute tolerance.
